chunks: Sahl, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musanna, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem with a man wearing Ihram while his weapon is upon him, if he fears the enemy.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah, involving specific clothing and prohibitions.
key_terms.بَأْس: Problem, difficulty, or harm; used here in the negative 'la ba'sa' to indicate permissibility.
key_terms.سِلَاح: Weapon, specifically referring to items like swords or shields carried for protection.
key_terms.عَدُوّ: Enemy, referring to potential attackers or hostile forces.

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim wear a weapon while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: Reported through the chain of Zurarah, a key link in the transmission of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir’s jurisprudence, this hadith clarifies that the prohibition on carrying weapons during Ihram is not absolute but contingent upon the risk of enemy attack. It illustrates the Shia principle of *darura* (necessity) overriding general prohibitions, ensuring the pilgrim's safety remains paramount during the sacred state.

en.hubeali:
Sahl, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Musna, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem with it if the man were to wear Ihraam and upon him is his weapon, when he fears the enemy’.
en.sarwar: 4. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muthanna’ from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
it is not harmful to carry arms in the state of Ihram if a man is afraid of the enemy. ‘“
